results.instruction: Wash the cucumbers well and cut out any damaged parts.
Cut the cucumbers into quarter inch slices and put them in the bowl.
Sprinkle them with a third of cup of salt and toss with your hands.
Now cover the vegetables with ice cubes and let them stand at room temperature for three hours.
Pour off the liquid and remove the garlic cloves.
Sterilize your jars by sterilizing them for one minute in boiling water.
Fill a canner 2/3 full of water.
Put the lid on and start heating it up.
Sterilize the lids by putting them in a bowl of boiling water for at least a minute.
Using a pot that will be big enough to fit all the vegetables, make the grind by combining the vinegars, sugar and spices.
Heat just to a boil.
Then add the drained vegetables and simmer them together for 10 minutes.
Using the measuring cup or ladle, fill the sterilized jars with the vegetables and brine to within an inch of the top of the jar.
Use a chopstick to poke around and release any air bubbles.
Then top each jar with a little more brine so the level is about three quarters of an inch from the top of the jar.
Wipe the top of each jar very carefully with a damp paper towel to remove any drips or bits of cucumber.
Wipe the top of each jar very carefully with a damp paper towel to remove any drips or bits of cucumber.
Ensure the rims are completely clean and dry, then dry each lid and set one on top of each of the clean jar rims.
Screw the rings on loosely, not tightly.
Use the jar lifter to lower each jar into the hot water, keeping the jars upright.
When the counter is full, add more hot water, put the cover on and turn up the heat.
Once the water comes to a vigorous boil, set the timer for 10 minutes.
When the timer rings, turn off the heat.
Use the jar lifter to remove one jar at a time, keeping the jars upright, not tilted.
Place them on towels or a cooling rack and let them sit undisturbed for 12 to 24 hours.
Check that all the jars have sealed by tapping on the lids.
They should have a ping and not a thud.
Wipe the jars with a damp cloth to remove any sticky residue from the jars.
Store them away in a cool dry place out of direct flight.
